races.name: Welcome To Family Day Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tiny Riot
runners_data.note: The Dan Skelton–Harry Skelton combination is a powerful pointer at this level; Tiny Riot won over 16f on Good last time and is the only runner with a victory in this field, with its hold-up style perfectly matched to a sprint-finish scenario on Good to Firm ground and just 30 days between runs keeping it race-sharp.|
runners_data.comment: Tiny Riot ran a solid race to finish runner-up last time out, having scored two starts back - a pair of efforts that mark him the main threat here. He has raced over today's distance before, is fit from a 30-day break, and his trainer is among the form, landing 12 of the last 24; he rates 88, second on our figures.

runners_data.name: Hello Garda
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground form across five runs but has never won in any of them, and the fading-in-finish flag combined with a 15-furlong gap since last seen means stamina for 2m½f is genuinely untested; its true rear-of-field preference is constrained here by the number of hold-up types in this small field, reducing its ability to find the gap it needs late.|
runners_data.comment: Hello Garda is having his first run under rules, so there's nothing on the board yet to judge him by. Carrying 154 lb, he's unexposed and could easily improve with racing, but it's simply too hard to know how competitive he'll be on debut.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Mo
runners_data.note: A string of bottom-half finishes on Southwell's all-weather (tenth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth) paints a bleak picture for a switch to Stratford turf on Good to Firm; 76 days off the track adds another layer of doubt, and though its natural game is to race from behind, the lack of any live finishing burst in recent outings makes it hard to construct a winning scenario even if the shape fits.|
runners_data.comment: Just Call Me Mo makes his racecourse debut here with no form to work from. He carries 154 lb and, like most first-time runners, is hard to assess — the form book will only start to build after this experience.

runners_data.name: Lucky Sevens
runners_data.note: Four places from five runs including a win over 10f Good and a second over 16f Good last time out show consistent turf form on the correct going, and with trainer James Owen striking at 10/57 over 14 days Jonathan Burke can send this horse forward to fill the pace vacuum; the headgear worn previously is worth monitoring if applied today as it may sharpen its early keenness.|
runners_data.comment: Lucky Sevens is yet to win but was a solid runner-up last time out, a form line that makes him the pick of a moderate four on our figures at 94. He returns quickly on a 13-day break and already has today's distance and going covered — a shallow form book is the only slight worry.

races.paceDynamic: With all four runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 2m½f juvenile hurdle at Stratford on Good to Firm ground is set to be run at a muddling, conservative tempo until the field wakes up in the straight. The absence of any natural pace-setter means the early gallop will almost certainly be tardy, with Harry Skelton likely nursing Tiny Riot off the back, Jonathan Burke likely to send Lucky Sevens forward from his prominent habits, and Hello Garda and Just Call Me Mo finding themselves shuffled into midfield positions that don't reflect their natural inclinations. The race will compress into a bunched sprint finish from the second-last hurdle, with the emphasis firmly on horses that can travel smoothly through a slow pace and produce a sharp, decisive turn of foot in the final two furlongs. This shape overwhelmingly favours hold-up runners with genuine jumping accuracy and a sprint-finish pedigree — specifically those with proven form on Good to Firm ground and recent racecourse sharpness. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Tiny Riot, with its superior class profile and Skelton partnership, is best placed to exploit a late run, while Lucky Sevens — the only runner with a win on Good ground over a longer trip — is most likely to have secured a prominent berth from which to dictate terms if any runner dares to.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and bunches, forcing a sprint from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing to lead, pace will be falsely slow and the field compact entering the straight, meaning jumping fluency and a sharp finishing kick become decisive. Tiny Riot's strong finishing form (two runs, a second and a win over 16f on Good) and the Skelton partnership give it the profile to pounce from behind in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lucky Sevens Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Lucky Sevens is sent forward by Jonathan Burke to fill the pace vacuum and dictates from the front.
scenarios.body: Burke, on a horse with a prominent inclination masked by a hold-up label and recent second over 16f Good, could exploit the absence of any natural front-runner to bowl along at a comfortable clip, making all. Winning from the front on Good to Firm at Stratford on a flat track suits a horse that has placed four times in five runs and won over 10f on Good.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Flatten Out
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop picks up mid-race and those forced out of their natural hold-up position fade in the straight.
scenarios.body: Hello Garda and Just Call Me Mo, both tagged as runners who fade in finish and who carry STYLE_FIT penalties for racing out of role, would struggle if the race develops early enough to expose their stamina limitations over 2m½f on quick ground. In this shape, the runners best placed are those with tactical adaptability and sound jumping rather than a pure finishing burst — Tiny Riot's class advantage still applies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp the Front
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Garda or Just Call Me Mo find an unusually clean run from midfield and produce a late surge.
scenarios.body: Both horses are redistibuted true hold-up types with fading tendencies in finish and neither has won in five and ten runs respectively — this scenario depends on a near-perfect trip and rivals making errors at the last. The combination of poor recent form (Just Call Me Mo finishing 10th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th on Southwell) and Hello Garda's consistent back-end fade makes this the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Lucky Sevens at the start — if Jonathan Burke sends it forward immediately into the pace vacuum, it could control this race from the front and prove very difficult to peg back on Good to Firm ground over 2m½f.

Tiny Riot's hold-up profile requires a clean run from the back in a field of only four; any crowding or slow-jumping rival directly ahead could cost it the room it needs to deliver its late challenge.

Hello Garda's fading-in-finish tendency is a live risk in a sprint scenario — if the race quickens sharply from the second-last, watch for it to be flattening out rather than staying on through the final hurdle.

Just Call Me Mo returns from 76 days off and switches from Southwell all-weather to Stratford turf — monitor its paddock demeanour and early jumping for any sign it has trained on, as a fresh run on fast ground is a significant change of environment from its recent form string.

races.name: Next Sunday Is Ladies Day Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Brionywells
runners_data.note: Best OR (91) in the field with back-to-back wins on good ground over 20-23f, ridden by claiming jockey Nick Slatter (3lb), 30 days fresh — strong form profile suits the likely sprint-finish shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Stavanger Rose
runners_data.note: Recent form reads UF-640, no wins or places from seven runs at this going, and Tabitha Worsley takes the ride for a trainer with just one runner in the past fortnight — very hard to trust despite holding up style being theoretically suited.

runners_data.name: Bits Ballou
runners_data.note: Showed a place at 26f on good ground which is directly relevant to today's trip, but is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a mapped midfield position; style-fit penalty tempers expectations despite Sam Twiston-Davies being a significant jockey booking.

runners_data.name: Son Of Tyran
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on good ground with Harry Skelton aboard and carries the in-form Skelton yard's T14 strike rate (11/26), but a noted tendency to fade in the finish is a real concern in what will likely be a sprint, and headgear (blinkers) suggests the stable knows it.

runners_data.name: French Diablo
runners_data.note: Only four runs in, placed at 22f on good ground which is encouraging at this trip, wears a hood and was last seen just 13 days ago — a natural closer shuffled toward midfield in the race map, so any winning chance requires this young horse to adapt its approach under David Bass.

runners_data.name: Babychino
runners_data.note: Amateur claimer Sophie Carter (7lb) on board for a small operation, and this four-year-old's form of P53 over 16-20f includes a place — trips shorter than today's 21f+ suggest the extra distance is unknown; mapped to midfield despite hold-up tendencies.

runners_data.name: League Clash
runners_data.note: Returning from a massive 671-day absence, which almost entirely overshadows any other factor — wears a tongue tie, has placed at 26f on good ground which suits the trip, but trainer has 0 from 6 in the last fortnight and the layoff is a massive red flag.

runners_data.name: Pink Walls
runners_data.note: Lowest OR (62) in the field and form of P0-P8 shows no completed finishes of note; wears a hood, last ran 26 days ago, and all five recent runs were over distances shorter than today's 21f — stamina at 2m6f is unproven and this is a very weak profile.

races.paceDynamic: This 2m6f contest on Good to Firm ground at Stratford is a field of eight confirmed hold-up types with no genuine front-runner in the lineup, meaning the early gallop is likely to be modest and tactical, with horses jostling for position without anyone willing to make a decisive move. The pace map's note is critical: Bits Ballou, Son Of Tyran, French Diablo, Babychino, League Clash, and Pink Walls are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because there are simply more horses wanting to race off the pace than the map can accommodate at the rear — none of these is a natural front-runner who will go and make it. With no pace injection from the front, this race will almost certainly crawl for the first mile and a half before turning into a sprint-finish hurdle dash over the final two furlongs, rewarding horses with a sharp turn of foot rather than relentless galloping ability. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: horses capable of travelling well in a slowly-run race and producing a late, powerful finish are massively advantaged, while stamina-reliant grinders will find themselves undone by the insufficient tempo and the resulting sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Crawl Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles through the early stages and the race becomes a furlong-and-a-half dash from the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian gallop sets up a sprint finish where positioning off the final turn and a sharp acceleration become decisive, suiting Brionywells whose hold-up style and recent win form in good going are tailor-made for this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Steadies
scenarios.trigger: If a slightly stronger middle-mile pace filters out the lesser stayers and the race becomes a genuine test of class from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Horses with the higher OR and best recent form in similar conditions are best placed to absorb a modest step-up in tempo and sustain their effort, with Brionywells and Son Of Tyran best credentialled on OR and recent winning form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types successfully sneaks a prominent position and controls the race from the front at a sedate clip.
scenarios.body: This outcome requires a horse racing completely out of its natural role — unlikely given the field composition — but French Diablo or Babychino at lighter weights could benefit from a surprise forward move, though their style-fit discounts make this a low-probability shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a freak of a false pace creates a single devastating late burst won by the widest-margin closer in the field.
scenarios.body: Stavanger Rose's hold-up profile and track familiarity with distance give theoretical coverage here, while League Clash's return from 671 days off adds significant unknown variance, but both carry form concerns that make this the least reliable shape.

watchPoints.text: Brionywells is the form pick here — watch whether Nick Slatter (3lb claim) can settle this hold-up type quietly before delivering a late challenge, because if the horse travels sweetly the OR superiority and recent winning form make it a genuine danger.

Son Of Tyran's tendency to fade in the finish combined with a sprint-finish setup is a key contradiction — watch whether Harry Skelton opts for an earlier-than-usual challenge to counter the finishing fade, which could dramatically change how the race unfolds.

League Clash is returning from 671 days off and must be treated as a significant unknown — watch the betting market and paddock closely, as any market confidence for this horse would carry unusual significance given the layoff.

With no genuine front-runner, watch which jockey blinks first and moves forward to ensure a lead — any horse pressing into the front two in the early stages will have adopted a role entirely different from its form profile, altering the scenario map materially.

French Diablo's hood and David Bass booking for a 4-year-old with limited hurdling experience at 2m6f is worth monitoring — if Bass allows this horse to creep into a prominent early position, the scenario probabilities shift meaningfully toward SCENARIO_C.

races.name: Gary Hubball's 60th Celebration Year Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton's five-year-old has placed twice over course-relevant distances on Good ground recently, sits on a workable OR of 100, and should travel prominently without needing to lead — the honest tempo suits a horse that has been knocking on the door in this sort of company.

runners_data.name: Aslukgoes
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with 9/13 sim-going record and four career wins; carries a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting it is effectively racing out of its ideal role (it is the pace-maker here, not chasing), but the absence of any challenger for the lead is a genuine asset — the risk is it gets picked off on the run-in.

runners_data.name: Artiste D'ainay
runners_data.note: Billy Aprahamian's eight-year-old won over 24f on Good ground and has strong course form at this trip; races prominently and jumps well enough to hold a handy position — headgear (tongue tie) is noted and the 11-day turnaround is short but connections ran it fresh before.

runners_data.name: Royal Time
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes over on this hold-up horse which has placed over 22f on Good and third over 20f on Soft — the 52-day absence is the key query, but the form at this sort of distance on quick ground is solid and Tudor is a high-quality booking.

runners_data.name: My Lovely Horse
runners_data.note: A six-year-old hold-up type with a modest sim-going record (0W0P on comparable ground) and a 5lb claimer; no obvious form flag screaming involvement, and the OR of 75 reflects limited ceiling, though 29-day break is not an issue.

runners_data.name: Frankie Faulkner
runners_data.note: Has placed three times on Good including a second over this distance on Good; a natural hold-up horse bumped to an effective midfield mapping because the rear of the field is crowded — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) tempers enthusiasm, and 67 days off is worth noting at OR 73.

runners_data.name: Shuile Warrior
runners_data.note: 85 days off the track and only one run on comparable going in five recorded starts (nothing placed on Good); Paddy Hanlon's 5lb claim helps the weight, but the layoff combined with going concerns makes this an each-way proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Rockvale
runners_data.note: Robert Dunne rides a horse whose natural instinct is to race from behind — placed to midfield on the map because hold-up ground is scarce in this field; has a second over 21f on Good and consistent course-trip form, but the 0W1P sim-going record and STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) means it needs things to fall right.

runners_data.name: Miss Pearl
runners_data.note: David Rees's 10-year-old has placed once on Good over 20f and is a genuine hold-up type slotted into a midfield position by necessity given the volume of similar operators in this race; at OR 72 and age 10 the ceiling is clear, though Shane Fenelon's 5lb claim assists.

runners_data.name: Citizen Jane
runners_data.note: Ryan Potter's five-year-old has won twice on Good recently (including back-to-back at 20f), but those came on Soft-bottomed Good ground and the current Going to Firm is a step quicker than anything in its recent profile; true hold-up style pushed closer to midfield here — STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) applies and the 13-day turnaround is brisk.

races.paceDynamic: Aslukgoes is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner novices' handicap chase over 2m6½f on Good to Firm ground at Stratford, and with no rival likely to seriously press for the lead, Mickey Bowen's eight-year-old should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a lung-bursting test. The pace will be genuine but not frantic — a single leader setting a sustainable tempo over this distance on quick ground is the classic recipe for a race that plays into the hands of horses travelling smoothly in behind, allowing them to close methodically from the second half of the race. The field nominally contains several hold-up types — Rockvale, Frankie Faulkner, Miss Pearl, and Citizen Jane are all mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is simply too congested to reflect their true preference — but those redistributed horses are unlikely to get a clean, deep hold-up position and will race closer than ideal. This race shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a measured pace — favours hold-up or prominent horses that can travel fluently in the mid-to-rear group and produce a sustained finish in the straight, with those carrying class (Laffer Curve, Artiste D'ainay, Royal Time) best placed to exploit the honest but not punishing tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aslukgoes Dictates, Closers Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Aslukgoes leads uncontested at a fair but unextended gallop and the race only truly ignites from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Aslukgoes sets every fraction without a challenge, creating a truly-run race at a pace that suits horses travelling smoothly in the chasing pack; the straight becomes a stamina test on quick ground where class and clean jumping tell.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace drops sufficiently in the middle sector to compress the field and create a sprint finish from the last.
scenarios.body: A muddling, stop-start tempo would allow the genuine hold-up types — Frankie Faulkner, Miss Pearl — to close sharply if they can find a clear run, though their redistributed positions make securing a true back-of-field berth uncertain.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just testing enough to pop rivals on the second circuit and a prominent horse goes clear before the last.
scenarios.body: Artiste D'ainay has the course form at this sort of trip and likes to race with cover before asserting; if the leader weakens after the third-last, a horse sitting second or third could go clear and not be caught.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Leader Survives on Quick Ground
scenarios.trigger: If Aslukgoes finds the Good to Firm ground playing to its advantage and the field behind over-commits chasing it.
scenarios.body: Quick ground and a solo lead can occasionally allow a front-runner to steal an unassailable advantage if those in behind mistime their challenge; Aslukgoes has course-and-distance form and four wins to its name, so the upset is live if rivals are flat.

watchPoints.text: Laffer Curve — Harry Skelton rides a horse with two recent placed efforts on Good ground at similar distances; if the Skelton operation has it right at the handicap mark, this is the most dangerous closer once Aslukgoes is headed.

Aslukgoes — the sole pace-setter faces no pressure on the lead, but its STYLE_FIT flag indicates it is performing outside its comfort zone as front-runner; watch for it to tire sharply from the second-last if the quick ground takes a toll.

Citizen Jane — two recent wins look enticing but both came on softer variants of Good; Good to Firm is a new test for this five-year-old and if it fails to handle the ground its hold-up style becomes a liability rather than an asset.

Rockvale, Frankie Faulkner, Miss Pearl — all three are natural hold-up types pushed forward on the map; watch the early stages to see whether any of them actually manage to get to the rear of the field, as that would increase their relevance materially in the straight.

Royal Time — the 52-day absence for Jack Tudor's mount is the one factual unknown in an otherwise tidy profile; watch how it travels in the first mile — if it jumps fluently and Tudor has it travelling strongly, the layoff concern dissolves quickly.

races.name: University Hospitals Birmingham Charity Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gambino
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's progressive five-year-old has the clearest form claims at the head of affairs on good ground, has won over this trip before, and Harry Skelton will use his positional advantage to set a race-controlling tempo; a style-fit flag notes he is technically racing into a slightly unfamiliar role but the evidence of his recent form suggests he handles it better than most.

runners_data.name: Haderach
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator whose hurdles form reads PP-U with a fades-in-finish flag and a 68-day absence; the combination of a return from a lengthy layoff, poor finishing record, and an amateur jockey booking makes it hard to see how he enters calculations even if the pace sets up for closers.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's six-year-old arrives on the back of a 12-day turnaround and showed genuine placed form over 18f on good ground recently, suggesting the trip is well within range; his true style is a back-of-the-field operator, but with the rear congested he is likely pushed into a midfield berth that is less comfortable for him.

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for the Twiston-Davies yard who has been consistently placed in staying hurdles without winning, with five runs on good ground and two placed efforts over 16f; holds up by preference but, with several rivals forced even wider at the rear, he may end up fractionally better positioned than usual and represents one of the more credible threats to the leader.

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old has posted three runs reading 5-7-7, suggesting he has not yet found his level or jumping confidence, and while the trainer's yard is in fine form, this runner's hold-up tendency means he is pushed into midfield where his actual race record offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for the in-form Faye Bramley yard, and this four-year-old's recent placed second at 16f on good ground is the most compelling piece of recent form outside the favourite's; a genuine hold-up type placed into midfield against his instincts, his best chance depends on the pace being fast enough to string the field out and allow him a clean run.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: Carries the fades-in-finish flag alongside a 26-day gap since last seen, and his hurdles record shows a sole placed effort from four starts with a pulled-up finish at the end of that sequence; naturally a hold-up horse crowded into midfield, and the finishing tendency flag is a significant barrier to him getting involved at the business end.

races.paceDynamic: Gambino is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of seven and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the off, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout this 2m½f maiden hurdle on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. The remainder of the field — Haderach, Penzance, Usyk, Delgany Second Now, Genealogy, and Angel Of My Dreams — are all hold-up or back-end types, meaning Gambino faces zero early pressure and can set whatever fractions suit Dan Skelton's patient race-riding plan under Harry Skelton. This race shape — a lone leader on a flat, right-handed track in a small field — classically rewards a horse that can control the tempo, conserve energy over the hurdles, and kick again at the business end. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can be accommodated at the rear, with Genealogy, Delgany Second Now, Penzance and Angel Of My Dreams all likely to be shuffled into an unnatural midfield berth rather than their preferred back positions, compromising their ability to produce a clean, late run. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: horses that can race prominently or track a controlled pace — and crucially, act off it — are clearly favoured over true closers who face a traffic and positional puzzle in a race that may not be truly run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gambino Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino bowls along unchallenged and Skelton dictates an honest but not suicidal tempo.
scenarios.body: Gambino leads from flag-to-finish on a flat track with zero pace pressure, jumping efficiently and conserving enough to stretch clear from the last; in a small field with no rival able to close the gap, a front-runner of his class and going preference is extremely hard to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino's pace is genuinely sustainable but one hold-up horse threads through traffic to nail him close home.
scenarios.body: A horse like Genealogy or Penzance, if they negotiate the midfield congestion cleanly, could swoop late on a tired leader at the last; this shape requires a perfect trip from a horse racing out of its natural role, which is the key execution risk.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino misjudges the fractions, goes too fast too soon, and weakens before the last flight.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting just off the pace — most likely a redistributed type who has managed to track Gambino at close quarters — would be best placed to inherit the lead and hold on; Usyk, with a hint of positional flexibility and previous placed form at this trip on good ground, would be a natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Unseated/Falls
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino exits the race through a jumping error, completely resetting the race shape.
scenarios.body: With no other natural front-runner in the field, the race degenerates into a muddled affair with horses jostling for a position none wanted; the horse who reacts fastest and seizes an unexpected lead — most likely the most versatile of the hold-up contingent — profits from the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Gambino's jumping at speed is the single biggest variable — if Harry Skelton allows him to dominate from the front cleanly, no other runner in this field has the profile to reel him in.

Genealogy and Harry Cobden combination is worth monitoring in running: if Cobden gets a clean, unobstructed passage from a midfield berth that is still closer than his natural position, his recent placed form makes him the most credible late challenger.

Angel Of My Dreams and Haderach both carry fades-in-finish flags — if either drifts wide or loses ground at a hurdle in the back straight, they risk being tailed off before the race enters its decisive phase.

With four horses (Penzance, Delgany Second Now, Genealogy, Angel Of My Dreams) all compressed into a midfield they would not naturally choose, monitor the second-last hurdle for crowding and interference — a single mistake there could decide second place.

Usyk's amateur jockey booking (Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell) in a race where positioning is non-negotiable adds a small but genuine execution risk; watch her reaction if Gambino builds a lead from the third-last.

races.name: Visit Zoolab In The Centre Course Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Person Of Interest
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden is a significant jockey booking for a 6-year-old on the upgrade; holds course form at similar going (sim-going 12/15) but natural hold-up style means relying on others to set the race up, and the 2m3½f trip looks within range of his recent runs around 2m.|
runners_data.comment: Person of Interest is winless in his last five starts, sixth last time out having been unseated the run before, so this is a modest springboard to top a weak book. Still, he edges it on our figures at 102, has raced over today's distance before, and returns from a 25-day break carrying 174 lb.

runners_data.name: Definite Dream
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter with a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting this prominent role is slightly out of character — however, with nobody to press, Denis Coakley's 8-year-old has every chance to find this role comfortable; wears tongue-tie and has nine runs on similar ground, going 0W5P but consistently placed.|
runners_data.comment: Definite Dream is without a win in her last four starts, but a second two starts back shows she stays competitive in this grade, and she rates a strong second on our figures at 102. She has both today's distance and going covered, returns from a 25-day break, and that modest scoreline remains the one query against her.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton combine with the highest-rated hold-up horse in the field (OR 95), and his recent form string 3-212 shows genuine consistency; headgear (tongue-tie and blinkers) sharpens him, and his 1W3P on similar going from three relevant runs is the best strike rate among the closers.|
runners_data.comment: Thickthorn Tom finished runner-up last time out, a winner two starts back, form that makes him a threat despite sitting only fourth on our figures at 92. He has raced over today's distance before, returns from a 23-day break, and his trainer is among the form, landing 10 of the last 27; his 95 official mark sits above our figure, the one query.

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's 9-year-old has been out just seven days — the quick turnaround is worth noting — and though shown in midfield on the map, this horse genuinely wants to come from off the pace; STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations if he cannot get back to his natural position, and a 0W3P similar-going record at OR 89 limits optimism.|
runners_data.comment: Applejack Poet is winless in his last five starts, sixth last time out, third two starts back, and a faller four starts back. He races over today's distance and returns quickly on a seven-day break, but a rating of 88, a shade below his 89 official mark, keeps him firmly in midfield.

runners_data.name: Boom Boom
runners_data.note: Rob Summers' 8-year-old arrives here on the back of a grim recent sequence (87P-PP) and, though two wins appear in his sim-going record (2W4P over 11 runs), those may be distant; genuinely wants to race from the back but the map places him in midfield, and the out-of-role concern is real given his current form.|
runners_data.comment: Boom Boom's recent form reads three straight pulled-up efforts, but our figures still rate him well clear of that at 99 — some way above his 83 official mark — hinting at untapped ability. He has both today's distance and going covered and returns from a 26-day break, though that run of unfinished races is impossible to ignore.

runners_data.name: Bahtiyar
runners_data.note: Max Young's 8-year-old carries just 148lbs and has a notably consistent placed record (2-4425, sim-going 0W6P over 14 runs) suggesting a horse that finds ways to be competitive without winning; wears a hood (hg:p) and the 39-day break is the longest in the field — hold-up style is genuine but the redistribution to midfield means he may not settle as well as he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Bahtiyar is winless in his last five starts and rates only sixth of seven on our figures at 85, leaving him hard to fancy. He does have both today's distance and going covered, and a pair of seconds in his recent starts show he's capable of running well, but a 39-day layoff adds a further question.

runners_data.name: Fox Wallace
runners_data.note: Ella Pickard has no 14-day runners logged and this 8-year-old on OR 69 has a recent form string of 6PP-P5 that offers little encouragement; absent 45 days and a true hold-up horse forced onto the map in midfield, Fox Wallace faces an uphill task tactically and on form alike.|
runners_data.comment: Fox Wallace is bottom of our figures here at 80 and her recent form does little to argue otherwise — three pulled-up efforts sandwiched by a fifth and a sixth. She does have today's distance and going covered, but a 45-day gap since her last run adds to the concerns.

races.paceDynamic: Definite Dream is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner handicap chase over 2m3½f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, and with no rivals likely to seriously contest the lead, Brendan Powell can dictate an entirely uncontested, sustainable gallop. The remaining field is composed overwhelmingly of hold-up types — Applejack Poet, Boom Boom, Bahtiyar, and Fox Wallace are all genuine sit-and-wait performers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there is no space for them at the rear in a race of this size and shape. Thickthorn Tom and Person Of Interest also operate from off the pace, meaning Definite Dream will likely face zero early pressure and can control every yard of the race. This race shape strongly favours a single prominent horse that can dictate its own terms and grind out a rhythm on fast ground — the danger comes not from pace rivals but from hold-up horses who can land close enough through the race to launch a late challenge, though the uncontested lead gives Definite Dream every opportunity to steal a march.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Definite Dream Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Definite Dream bowls along uncontested at a comfortable gallop and the hold-up pack is left with too much ground to make up at the finish.
scenarios.body: Brendan Powell sets a measured but consistent pace that suits the good-to-firm surface, and with no rivals willing or able to press, Definite Dream arrives at the last with enough in reserve to repel challengers; horses who prefer racing prominently benefit most here as the gap to cover from the rear proves too great.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Definite Dream's solo front-running tempo proves just fast enough to set up a strong late finish for a well-positioned hold-up runner.
scenarios.body: A horse who manages to travel closer than its natural style dictates — benefiting from the redistribution dynamic — gets into a winning position approaching the last and has the class to sustain a run to the line; Thickthorn Tom, trained by Dan Skelton and rated highest among the closers, is best placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Definite Dream sets too strong a gallop early on the quick ground and begins to tire from two out, leaving the field to come through.
scenarios.body: The hold-up brigade, spread across midfield through necessity rather than choice, suddenly find themselves in contention as the leader falters; Person Of Interest, who has course form and is well ridden by Harry Cobden, and Bahtiyar, with consistent placed form over this trip on similar ground, are most likely to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Finish, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down at the fences — through a fall, unseated rider, or a cluster of jumping errors — and the field bunches chaotically in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Fox Wallace or Boom Boom, both operating well below their natural comfort zone but still present, could stumble into frame in a muddled finish; this is strictly an accident-of-chaos scenario and carries no tactical rationale beyond survival.

watchPoints.text: Watch Definite Dream's jumping at the early fences — if Brendan Powell's front-runner makes errors and loses his rhythm, the entire race shape collapses and the hold-up pack inherits a race they would not normally be set up to win.

Monitor whether Thickthorn Tom (Harry Skelton) manages to travel closer than his hold-up tag suggests in the early stages — if the Skelton pair get him into a handy position tracking Definite Dream, his class advantage over this field becomes decisive.
Applejack Poet's seven-day turnaround is the shortest break in the field; watch for signs of fatigue or jumping errors in the closing stages if the quick reappearance has left him short of freshness.

With four horses all genuinely preferring to race from the rear (Applejack Poet, Boom Boom, Bahtiyar, Fox Wallace) but crammed into midfield on the map, there is a real risk of traffic and interference on the final bend — particularly if the pace drops and the field compresses behind Definite Dream.

Bahtiyar's hood (hg:p) is worth noting at the start — if he fails to settle early having been forced into a more forward position than his natural style demands, his finishing effort may be compromised over this 2m3½f trip on fast ground.

races.name: Try Our Picnic Package Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Paddy Hanlon who has placed 14 times from 15 similar-going runs, this seven-year-old's record on good ground is strong — but in a race with a single, controlled front-runner, he is reliant on the pace quickening enough late to bring his staying effort to bear, and his recent form (3-P-4-4-U) suggests he is finding winning harder.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and unseated last time out, War Correspondent still rates clear of his rivals on our figures at 128. Two fourths came before that, and he has raced over today's distance before, fit again from a 36-day break; a chunky 169 lb is the only reservation.

runners_data.name: Donnie Azoff
runners_data.note: The most compelling staying profile in the field — Jamie Snowden's ten-year-old has won over 22f on good ground and carries 13 wins or places from 15 similar-going runs — but Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim can only help so much when the race shape is likely to be slow-run, which is not what this thorough stayer needs to display his best at OR 119.
runners_data.comment: Donnie Azoff arrives in fine heart, winning last time out and twice in his last five starts, and sits second on our figures at 122 having raced over today's distance before. A blip when fifth three starts back is the only concern, but fitness from a 30-day break should suit.

runners_data.name: Snatch A Glance
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's six-year-old is the natural tracking horse in this race and has a clean nine-from-nine record on similar going, including a win and multiple places; freshened up on just 12 days' rest with Fern O'Brien claiming 5lb, she needs to settle smartly behind Edelak and pick up efficiently, as a combative front two would serve her better than being left to time her run in isolation.
runners_data.comment: Snatch A Glance was fourth last time out, following two thirds and a fall, having won five starts back. He returns quickly here just 12 days on and has raced over today's going before; a rating of 120 stands well clear of his 114 official mark, though that fall remains a concern.

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's lightly-raced four-year-old has won three straight over 16f on good ground and is the confirmed pace-setter here — his OR of 118 and Harry Skelton in the saddle make him the dominant tactical force in a five-runner field, though racing up to 18f for the first time introduces the only real doubt about whether his sharp, front-running style translates fully over this extra trip.
runners_data.comment: Edelak arrives on a hat-trick, unbeaten in his last three starts, with a second four starts back, and a sixth five starts back, his only blips before that. Fit from just a 14-day break and with today's going form under his belt, he rates 121 on our figures, a shade above his 118 official mark - a leading threat to the top pick.

runners_data.name: Getmetothemoon
runners_data.note: Anthony Honeyball's seven-year-old is a genuine front-runner by inclination but sits in midfield on the pace map because Edelak and Snatch A Glance are better positioned to claim those berths; add a 178-day layoff, a declining recent form string (1-6-3-4-6), and Chad Bament's 5lb claim, and the combination of being out of natural position and rustiness makes it very hard to make a case for him here.
runners_data.comment: Getmetothemoon is hard to fancy on figures, rating lowest of this five at 103, and a lengthy 178-day absence adds to the concerns after a sixth last time out. She does have both today's distance and going covered, though, and a win came five starts back, with a third only three back showing she retains some ability.

races.paceDynamic: Edelak (Harry Skelton) is the confirmed front-runner and will set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front in what is a small five-runner field — with no genuine rival to pressure him, he can dictate every fraction on good to firm ground at Stratford. Snatch A Glance is the only other horse with prominent tendencies who can realistically track Edelak, while War Correspondent and Donnie Azoff are natural hold-up types who will be anchored in the rear, forced to wait for a late gap to open. Getmetothemoon is a genuine prominent racer by nature but has been redistributed to midfield in the mapping because this field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure that position — Edelak and Snatch A Glance are both more likely to take up the early lead and second berth ahead of Getmetothemoon, whose 178-day absence adds further doubt. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting a measured pace — overwhelmingly favours front-to-prominent profiles who can conserve energy and kick decisively at the last, with patient hold-up horses needing a genuine injection of pace to deliver them, which an unforced tempo may not supply.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Edelak Leads, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak settles uncontested in front and the pace stays controlled through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Skelton allows Edelak to bowl along at his own rhythm on the good to firm ground, using his three consecutive wins over 16f as evidence he can sustain this gallop and find more at the death; with no genuine challenger for the lead, he preserves energy for the climb to the final flight and the hold-up horses simply have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pair Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to stretch Edelak and Snatch A Glance, leaving the closers with a true target.
scenarios.body: Donnie Azoff, a winner over 22f on good ground and a horse with four wins and eight places from 13 similar-going runs, carries the most convincing late profile in this field and would relish a faster-run race that brings his stamina into play; War Correspondent is similarly held up by design but needs the leaders to overcook it, which given Skelton's tactical acuity is unlikely.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind, Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Snatch A Glance pushes the gallop alongside Edelak and the race becomes a slog, rewarding pure stamina over tactical speed.
scenarios.body: Snatch A Glance's record of nine runs on similar going — all competitive — and a win over 16f suggests she handles this surface well, and if she cranks the pace up from the front it may compromise Edelak while also bringing Donnie Azoff into contention late; this scenario requires Fern O'Brien to commit aggressively early, which is the less natural instinct for a 5lb claimer in a small field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or interference disrupt the front two and the race fragments unpredictably.
scenarios.body: Getmetothemoon is the only beneficiary of a chaotic scenario, having won over 16f on good ground before a lengthy 178-day absence, and a muddled race in which rivals cancel each other out could mask his fitness concerns; however, his style fit is compromised by redistribution, his last run was a blank, and this shape should only be considered in genuinely extreme circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Watch Edelak's jumping closely — a front-runner who makes even one significant error at a hurdle could instantly hand the initiative to Snatch A Glance and fundamentally reshape the race.

Donnie Azoff's chances hinge entirely on pace — if War Correspondent's rider (Paddy Hanlon) or Isabelle Ryder on Donnie Azoff do not attempt to inject pace from behind, the race could simply drift into a slow-run procession that suffocates both hold-up horses.
Getmetothemoon's 178-day absence is a significant fitness flag — monitor in the betting for any market drift that confirms trainer confidence has not strengthened ahead of the race.

Snatch A Glance is the key bridging horse to watch at the top of the home straight — if she challenges Edelak's lead two out rather than tracking patiently, the race tempo will spike and the dynamic for the closers changes materially.

Three of the five runners carry 5lb claiming jockeys, which could introduce inexperience in tactical decision-making — watch for positional errors in the early stages that force horses wider or into unexpected positions before the first flight.

races.name: Sun Racing The Favourite Pullout Every Day Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Miss Kassiopi
runners_data.note: Won over C&D equivalent 9 days ago under Harry Skelton for the in-form Dan Skelton stable (9/29 14-day strike rate); wears headgear, is pace-confirmed at the front, and her similar-going record of 2 wins from 15 runs suggests she competes consistently here — the STYLE_FIT flag simply reflects the tag applied at a generic level, not a true concern given her form is built racing prominently.
runners_data.comment: Miss Kassiopi has won twice in her last five starts, including last time out, though a seventh three starts back shows some inconsistency. She has raced over today's distance before, is fit from just a nine-day break, and her trainer is among the form, landing 9 of the last 29 (31% in the past fortnight) — but her 96 rating sits a little below her 102 official mark, capping her claims in this deep field.

runners_data.name: Pure Logic
runners_data.note: Consistent performer on good ground with five places from five recent starts but no wins in that sequence; Paddy Hanlon claims 5lb which helps at OR 101, though the Hanlon stable has only 1 win from 11 over the past 14 days — a horse that needs the race to come to it rather than one who can force the issue.
runners_data.comment: Pure Logic is winless in her last five starts, but a battling third last time out, matching her form from five starts back, is enough to top this moderate eight on our figures at 99. She has raced over today's distance before and returns quickly on just a 10-day break; the lack of a win in that spell is the only concern.

runners_data.name: Basilette
runners_data.note: Daniel Sansom claims 3lb for a Mullins yard that has been quiet (0/4 in 14 days), but Basilette's form string of 2114 shows a consistent winning type who handles good ground well; the step back from 16f to a longer 18f trip here suits, and prominent tactics mean she should be in the firing line throughout.
runners_data.comment: Basilette strung together back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and though two fourths have followed since, that spell of form makes her a live threat on our figures at 98. She has both today's distance and going covered, returns from just a 13-day break, and her official mark of 99 confirms she's fully up to this grade.

runners_data.name: La Lolita
runners_data.note: Returning from 252 days off which is the longest layoff in the field — a significant fitness concern for a four-year-old; her form includes a win over 21f on good ground last time out, so the trip is no issue, and James Bowen is a capable rider, but the layoff makes her a difficult proposition to assess with confidence.
runners_data.comment: La Lolita won two starts back and has generally held her form, with a third last time out and another third four starts back, plus a fifth in between. She has raced over today's going before, though a lengthy 252-day layoff since her last run is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: A Tickatickatiming
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has finished 4th and 5th in her last two starts; her similar-going record is modest at 7/15 and she has never won on good-to-firm, which is a concern given today's conditions — Marc Goldstein rides and at OR 90 she needs the race to fall apart in front of her to get involved.
runners_data.comment: A Tickatickatiming is winless in her last five starts, including a pulled-up effort three starts back, yet she rates a close second on our figures at 99 — well above her 90 official mark, suggesting real improvement. She has both today's distance and going covered and returns from just a 13-day break, with that pulled-up run the main query.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: Veterans of 13 races on good ground with 2 wins and 7 places, Quick Of The Night brings solid course-form credentials for Dave Roberts; despite the quiet trainer strike rate (0/1 in 14 days), this nine-year-old is reliable and consistent if outpaced at the business end — a place candidate more than a winner on current ratings.

runners_data.name: Sadies Diamond
runners_data.note: 370 days off the track is the most alarming flag in this field for a five-year-old; her form line of 28/28 shows ability to place but never to dominate, and Jack Stenhouse's 7lb claim helps offset the weight, though ring-rustiness from such a lengthy absence makes her extremely hard to trust at this level on comeback.
runners_data.comment: Sadies Diamond is winless in her last four starts and has been well beaten in three of them, leaving her second-bottom on our figures at 88. A second two starts back shows she has ability, and she has raced over today's distance before, but a lengthy 370-day absence makes her hard to trust fresh.

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: Good recent hurdle form includes a second on soft ground, but today's good-to-firm conditions are drier than her best performances; her true nature as a hold-up horse means she's been pushed into midfield on the map by the crowded rear — Robert Dunne will struggle to get her into a late run if the field doesn't string out properly.
runners_data.comment: Yanka Blue is winless in her last five starts, fifth last time out following a run of 6th, 6th and 9th, with a second her only bright spot five starts back. She has both today's distance and going covered, returns quickly on a 12-day break, and rates 93 on our figures — well clear of her 77 official mark, though the wider record keeps her only a midfield claim.

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: A chequered form line including pulls-up and unseated rider marks recent history; Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim is useful, but her best ground form (1 win, 2 places) came on softer surfaces and good-to-firm represents an untested scenario — her genuine hold-up style is displaced to midfield here, compounding the tactical difficulty of landing a blow.
runners_data.comment: Miss Fedora sits bottom of our figures at 83 and her recent form does little to inspire, with a pulled-up run and a refusal among her last five starts. She does have both today's distance and going covered and returns quickly on a 13-day break, but this looks a tough spot to find much improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Kassiopi is the lone confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine pressing rival to her inside or outside, she is likely to stride into a clear lead from the outset and control tempo on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Pure Logic, Basilette, and Quick Of The Night will compete for prominent positions behind her, creating a three-way tussle for the early cover slots that could string the field out from the second flight. The resulting race shape — a measured, uncontested lead with a busy group tracking two to four lengths back — strongly favours prominent-to-leading types who can sit in behind Miss Kassiopi without burning too much energy and then press from the home turn. This field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear: Yanka Blue and Miss Fedora are both true hold-up operators that have been mapped into midfield, but with three prominent types filling early positions, they are unlikely to find the gaps or ground to make their natural late runs count — Miss Kassiopi and Basilette are best placed to exploit the shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kassiopi Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi leads unchallenged and sets a sensible gallop that tests stamina without burning out the field.
scenarios.body: Miss Kassiopi dictates from the front on ground that suits her, and the horse who tracks her most economically through the final mile lands the decisive blow at the last; this shape rewards prominent racers with sound jumping and tactical awareness over the trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracking Group Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough to see Miss Kassiopi weaken approaching the home turn, promoting one of the trailing prominent runners.
scenarios.body: Pure Logic or Basilette, sitting a length or two off the leader through the back straight, seizes the initiative at the final flight as the leader flattens out; the good-to-firm surface rewards a horse that has been travelling smoothly throughout rather than one who has had to work hard early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Long-Trip Stayer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong early and the field strings out, allowing a hold-up horse with stamina to make significant late headway.
scenarios.body: La Lolita, whose best form includes a win over course-relevant distances on good ground, would be the primary beneficiary of a truly run race if she can navigate traffic from midfield; A Tickatickatiming is the secondary option on this shape but lacks the form ceiling to win outright at this level.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles The Order
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types clash for position early, causing jumping errors or a collapse in the pace that reshuffles the order entirely.
scenarios.body: A messy race in which several rivals are checked or crowded out would theoretically open the door for a redistributed hold-up horse like Yanka Blue or Miss Fedora to make a late run, but their STYLE_FIT concerns mean this scenario depends on a sequence of events heavily against the grain; this is the least likely shape and its probable beneficiaries are the least well-suited to delivering on it.

watchPoints.text: Miss Kassiopi (front-runner, Skelton/Skelton, 9 days since a win) is the key horse to watch at the start — if she jumps cleanly and secures the lead unchallenged, she controls the entire race shape.

Sadies Diamond (370-day layoff) and La Lolita (252-day absence) both return from lengthy breaks — monitor both in the preliminaries for signs of greenness or sweatiness that would signal they are unready to run to form.

Pure Logic, Basilette, and Quick Of The Night will all seek prominent positions early; if two or three of them push hard for cover behind the leader in the first half-mile, the tempo could spike and undermine the advantage of the front-runner.

Yanka Blue and Miss Fedora — genuine hold-up types remapped to midfield — should be tracked from the back straight to see whether they find racing room; if the field stacks up, their late runs may never materialise and they should be discounted from winning calculations.

Ground confirmation at Good To Firm throughout the card at Stratford is faster than several of these mares have shown their best form on — particularly Miss Fedora and A Tickatickatiming, whose winning form leans toward softer conditions.
